plan: The analysis treats calibration rows only as stiffness priors, pivots each up/down threshold pair into a center c and half-width h, and fits the proposed h=h0−K L² and center-shift J(L) laws by least squares with leave-one-L-out validation. The key measured relation is that pair_A widths collapse almost identically after normalization: h/h0≈1−(L/7.9 cm)² for both rotors, supporting a common multiplicative lever-arm contraction. However, the state-dependent center shift J is also approximately quadratic in L for both rotors, not linear as the bias–stiffness duality assumes; rotor 1 already favors L² over L by cross-validated error, and rotor 2 is strongly quadratic. Rotor 2 reaches |J|>h near L≈3.7 cm, so its two other-state threshold loops become disjoint within the tested range, which is a concrete conditional prediction for intermediate mounting distances. Pair_B crossed springs flip the sign of J and greatly amplify it, but rotor 2’s width is much larger than pair_A’s, confounded with its much wider angular stops. Network_C exactly repeats an eight-state single-flip cycle in the 16 events, but naive amplitude-row deletion creates multi-flip transitions, so the predicted period-8 truncation is plausible but not confirmed by these data alone. The limitations are four lever arms, 0.1 cm threshold rounding, no independent repetitions, one pair_B mounting distance, and unknown network_C connectivity, stop angles, and reversal positions; all fits are exploratory and mechanism claims remain conditional.

plan: Working plan: keep the calibration rows strictly as stiffness priors, pivot every matched up/down threshold into a center c and half-width h, then test whether the two "channels" of the proposed duality share one geometric scaling with the lever arm rather than L versus L² as hypothesized. The decisive comparisons are nested fits (h and J against L, L², and against each other) scored by leave-one-out error, plus a dimensionless ratio q = J/(h0−h) that should be constant if a single spring-geometry channel generates both effects. I also extract the extrapolated collapse length where h→0, the lever length where |J| exceeds h (which opens a unidirectional-coupling band of width 2(|J|−h) in which the free rotor is slaved to the held rotor at fixed drive), and treat both as conditional predictions bracketed by existing L values. Pair_B is used only as a sign/magnitude ordinal test at a single L, with stop-angle normalization checked and any residual confound reported rather than explained away. Network_C is analysed as an ordered state sequence with no timestamps: I count single-flip transitions, exact period repetition, and — crucially — how many drive reversals the recorded drive values require, because a period-8 state cycle is not the same as a period-8 amplitude loop. All fits are labelled exploratory, and no mechanism is asserted from threshold arithmetic alone.
